actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Accepted for the class contract; a MuJoCo reset restores the model defaults (mj_resetData) and does not use a seed
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: reset

facts.text: The repository is an Isaac Gym reinforcement learning environment for HighTorque's legged robot and also integrates a sim-to-sim framework from Isaac Gym to MuJoCo
The README describes the MuJoCo-based sim-to-sim deployment as running humanoid/scripts/sim2sim.py with an exported policy
The sim-to-sim entry point is the module-level function run_mujoco(policy, cfg)
run_mujoco loads the model with mujoco.MjModel.from_xml_path, overrides model.opt.timestep with the configured dt, creates mujoco.MjData and calls mujoco.mj_step once before the loop
Every loop iteration writes the clipped PD torques to data.ctrl and advances the model with mujoco.mj_step
Sim2simCfg sets sim_config.dt to 0.001 s and sim_duration to 60.0 s, with decimation 10
The default non-terrain model path ends at resources/robots/pai_12dof/mjcf/pai_12dof without the .xml extension, so an importing caller must supply the explicit file path
The MuJoCo model is declared as pai_12dof_v2_0312
The model sets the physics timestep to 0.001 s
The default block makes joints limited and motors control-limited unless an element overrides it
The base is floating: the base_link body carries three slide joints and one ball joint
The two legs carry twelve named hinge joints with per-joint ranges on the cited lines
The actuator section declares twelve motor actuators, one per leg joint, each with ctrllimited=true and ctrlrange -200 to 200
setup.py install_requires lists isaacgym, mujoco==2.3.6, mujoco-python-viewer and the training stack; there is no serial, USB or VISA dependency

determinism.notes: the stand-in has no random draw and the bridge snapshots the whole integration state, so the same controls reproduce the same trajectory; the real MuJoCo engine was not run

gaps: the fake backend is a pure Python stand-in for the mujoco library: it parses the MJCF for the joint dimensions, the actuator control ranges and the option timestep, but its integration moves each actuated joint in proportion to its control value; it resolves no contact, friction, equality, tendon, actuator or sensor dynamics, so the deployed fake is F0 even though the MJCF and real MuJoCo would support F1
no mesh or texture of the model's meshdir is loaded and the floating base is not integrated; a ball joint's quaternion is kept at its identity value and the base slides do not move
MuJoCo itself was not importable where the gate ran, so no trajectory was compared with the real engine; the sim backend that imports mujoco was not run

the upstream sim2sim loop also performs policy inference, observation stacking, PD torque computation and rendering (humanoid/scripts/sim2sim.py:116-176); this driver exposes only the MuJoCo ctrl vector and integration state
the card's second model, resources/robots/pai_12dof/mjcf/pai_12dof_terrain.xml, is not served: one package serves the primary model (models[0])
no physical Pai robot is modelled and nothing was validated against hardware

measures.description: Declared native checkpoint. Integration profile restores the full native input vector; basic profile restores only advertised state plus actuator activation and exact native time. Neither profile certifies external callbacks, plugins, RNG or hardware fidelity.

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the integration state is kept and stays readable
